# John Meredith

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v5 c2 P25](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0025), [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001)</sub>
- **Status:** engaged  <sub>[v5 c34 P44](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0044), [v5 c35 P5](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Presbyterian minister at Glen St. Mary  <sub>[v5 c2 P7](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0007), [v5 c2 P8](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0008), [v5 c12 P8](../source/v05-c12.md#nw-v05-c12-p0008)</sub>
- **Titles:** Reverend  <sub>[v5 c2 P8](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0008), [v5 c4 P0](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0000)</sub>; Mr.  <sub>[v5 c2 P25](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0025), [v5 c4 P0](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Jack  <sub>[v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

John Meredith possesses clear-cut, ivory-pallid facial features and slender white hands that conceal a steel-like grip. He has high browed dark hair that often falls in uncared-for locks, alongside dreamy dark eyes. At times, he displays an odd, pale face and a cut lip or swollen eye.

_Sources: [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 c13 P4](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0004), [v5 c14 P12](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0012), [v5 c17 P58](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0058), [v5 c21 P11](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0011), [v5 c28 P26](../source/v05-c28.md#nw-v05-c28-p0026), [v5 c34 P44](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0044)_

## Personality

John Meredith is a gentle, scholarly dreamer who lives in a world of books, abstractions, and spiritual reflection. Underneath his shyness, aloofness, and reserve, he retains the heart of a boy and is deeply sincere. He is extremely absent-minded and prone to forgetfulness, often becoming so absorbed in reading or thought that he loses track of time, meals, and parish obligations. Though tender-hearted and deeply loving toward his family, he struggles with practical house management and parenting duties.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P40](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0040), [v5 c4 P0](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0000), [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c14 P0](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0000), [v5 c14 P21](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0021), [v5 c14 P37](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0037), [v5 c21 P2](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0002), [v5 c21 P10](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0010)_

## History

After the death of his wife Cecilia, John Meredith moved to Glen St. Mary as the new Presbyterian minister, bringing along his four children and an elderly relative, Aunt Martha, to manage the manse. Due to his intense scholarly absorption and absent-mindedness, he frequently neglected household affairs and occasionally missed parish duties, such as prayer meetings and weddings. He formed a warm, unreserved friendship with young Walter Blythe, and eventually met Rosemary West by a spring in Rainbow Valley. Over the autumn and winter, he regularly visited her home, falling deeply in love with her. He attempted to propose to Rosemary, but she unexpectedly asked for time to consider before sending a written refusal, leaving him crushed and heartbroken. Meanwhile, criticism from parishioners like Mrs. Alec Davis forced him to confront his failures as a parent, though he found himself incapable of corporally punishing his children when they misbehaved. When his son Carl fell gravely ill with pneumonia, and later when Una fainted in church, his deep devotion to his children was painfully tested. Ultimately, after receiving a note from Rosemary inviting him to meet at the spring, their romance was restored, leading to their engagement and upcoming honeymoon.

## Quotes

> I thank you for your kind intentions, Mrs. Davis, but I cannot give you my child.  <sub>[v5 c14 P21](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0021)</sub>
